headline: This law lets a remaining member of the Merit Systems Protection Board extend certain personnel-action stays when the board lacks a quorum.
what_it_does: The Merit Systems Protection Board hears appeals from federal employees about personnel actions such as firings or demotions. A stay pauses such an action while the case is reviewed. This law says that if the board does not have enough members to make a quorum, any remaining member may extend the length of a stay when the Special Counsel asks. The change applies only during the time the board lacks a quorum.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees facing personnel actions such as removal or demotion
who_it_affects.how: A stay that pauses a contested personnel action can be extended while the board lacks enough members to act.
The Special Counsel can ask a remaining board member to extend a stay when the board has no quorum.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that take personnel actions
who_it_affects.how: Contested personnel actions may stay on hold for longer periods when the board cannot reach a quorum.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted June 27, 2017, and applies while the Merit Systems Protection Board lacks a quorum.
